title: Lattice refinement of a triclinic crystal (with Bragg peaks)
purpose: Exercises the lattice-refinement loop of the `epsr` engine [@soper1996,@soper2005,@epsrmanual], a random search over the unit-cell parameters a, b, c, alpha, beta, gamma that keeps a trial lattice when the fit to the diffraction data improves. It is the route by which EPSR refines the cell of a crystalline sample together with its structure.
system: The triclinic S/O1 crystal of ex121 (588 tethered atoms, 7 × 7 × 6 cells of a, b, c = 4.3, 4.8, 5.4 Å, alpha, beta, gamma = 80°, 100°, 110°, 300 K); EPSR-test `.pcof`, weights and data used unchanged as numerical input. With Bragg peaks [@squires1978] the R-factor against the three data sets depends on the lattice; trial cells are drawn with step sizes 0.2 Å and 1° and rescaled to constant density.
inputs: `scripts/make_case.sh` regenerates the inputs (verified byte-identical). Keywords changed: `iinit 1`, `ntimes 2`, `qwidthqmax 0.02 3.0`, `mplicities 7 7 6`, `hklqmin 0.0 8.0 0.05`, `nlatrefine 3`, `latrefine 0.2 0.2 0.2 1.0 1.0 1.0`. `commands.txt`: `repeat 2`.
verification: Per the README, in pass 1 the trials of steps 1 and 2 are accepted and step 3 rejected; in pass 2 steps 1 and 3 are rejected and step 2 accepted. The refined lattice is written to the `.ato` (stored Fortran reference: 30.224 × 33.667 × 32.641 Å box edges) and read back in pass 2. Each step runs `atogen` + `gensq` + Bragg correction and six `ran1` calls, so any difference would shift the random sequence.
notes: Reproduced: `clatnew` is rescaled with `blatfac`; when the last trial is rejected the box is restored but S(Q) is not recomputed.
